chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad and Abdullah ibn Sinan, altogether, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It is befitting for the guardians of the deceased among you that they should announce to the brethren of the deceased his death, so that they may witness his funeral, pray over him, and seek forgiveness for him; thus, reward is recorded for them, and forgiveness is recorded for the deceased; and he (the announcer) earns reward for them and for what they earned for their deceased through seeking forgiveness.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَيِّتِ: Guardians or close relatives of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the proper procedure for announcing death and seeking forgiveness for the deceased in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the communal obligation of announcing death to facilitate collective supplication, emphasizing the interconnectedness of the living and the dead in the spiritual economy. It highlights that the reward for the deceased is not static but can be actively increased through the specific acts of attendance, funeral prayer, and intercessory forgiveness performed by their community.
